questions.q: According to this course's decision framework, what should primarily determine the choice between manual entry, FBDI, and ADFdi?
options: Whichever tool the consultant finds the most enjoyable to use
Volume, frequency, and who is doing the work
The day of the week the data needs to be loaded
Which tool has the nicest-looking Excel ribbon
questions.explain: This is the same three-question framework introduced in lesson 1 and reapplied throughout the course: how many rows, how often, and who performs the work.

questions.q: Why is bank statement loading described as 'always FBDI, never a manual or ADFdi candidate'?
options: Because bank statements never contain useful data
Because ADFdi cannot technically connect to Cash Management
Because it's a recurring feed of an externally produced file (like BAI2) from a bank, not something a person types in or edits interactively
Because manual entry is faster for bank statements
questions.explain: Bank statement data originates as an externally produced file from the bank on a recurring cadence — exactly the scenario FBDI is built for, with no natural fit for manual or ADFdi entry.

questions.q: Why is Receivables transaction loading described as 'almost always FBDI'?
options: Because Receivables has no ADFdi option available at all, under any circumstance
Because Receivables transactions are always exactly five rows
Because FBDI is required by law for all receivables transactions
Because receivables transaction volume typically originates from another system (billing, point-of-sale, subscription platforms) rather than from a person typing directly into Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Unlike journals or invoices where ad-hoc, interactive entry is common, receivables data overwhelmingly originates externally, making FBDI the dominant method.

questions.q: What is the next course in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path after FBDI & ADFdi?
options: REST APIs & Integration Fundamentals
Oracle Fusion Security
Troubleshooting Oracle Financials
SQL for Oracle Financials
questions.explain: REST APIs & Integration Fundamentals is the next course in the Data Loading & Integrations stage, covering the fourth data-loading 'door' — system-to-system integrations.

questions.q: Which recurring idea from this course applies to BOTH FBDI and ADFdi, regardless of which tool is used?
options: Data must always pass through a ZIP file before being validated
A rejected row with a recorded reason is a solvable problem, and the discipline is to fix and resubmit only what actually failed
Every load must be manually re-typed at least once
Only FBDI ever produces rejected rows; ADFdi never does
questions.explain: This discipline — treating a rejection as a traceable, fixable issue and resubmitting only the corrected scope — was shown to apply to both FBDI (Chapter 5) and ADFdi (lesson 27).
